scenario: AITA for not painting my step father in a family picture? | I wanted to do something nice for my mom for her birthday, so I decided to paint her a picture. I oil paint as a hobby. I made a really sweet picture, I don’t want to post it here because it’s personal, but it was a picture of my mom smiling and holding my younger brother, as my dad pushed me on the swing in the background. It took me like 6 weeks or so to finish this painting. I gave it to my mom, and she cried she loved it. My parents aren’t together anymore but they were good friends until my mom met my step dad. First thing he said when she opened the painting was, “well, where am I?” This pissed me off and I ignored it but he kept going, saying if I needed a reference picture I could have asked him, and calling me rude and “exclusionary” because he’s a part of the family too and kept going on and on. My mom scolded me for being rude, and asked me to apologize for not putting him in the painting. WHAT? I still haven’t said a word to this man, it’s been about three weeks. My mom also hasn’t hung the picture up which really hurts my feelings. AITA?

The picture included their mom, younger brother, and dad (presumably the biological father) in the background. He even accused the person of being rude and exclusionary because he felt he was part of the family too. The person responded by saying they didn't paint him because they couldn't stand to look at his face for that long. That led to an argument, and now there's been no communication for about three weeks. The mom is upset too, asking the person to apologize for not including the stepfather. So, is it right or wrong to exclude someone from a family picture like this? Let's consider different perspectives. From the person's perspective, they put a lot of time and effort into the painting, and they wanted to include the people they felt were important to their mom. They might have had personal reasons for not wanting to include the stepfather, especially if there's tension or if they don't get along well. From the stepfather's perspective, he feels excluded and hurt. He might believe that as part of the family, he deserves to be included in such a meaningful gift. His reaction could stem from feeling unappreciated or undervalued. From the mom's perspective, she's caught in the middle. She's upset with the person for being rude and for excluding the stepfather, which suggests she might value the stepfather's role in the family. Now, considering the broader context, family dynamics can be complicated. Each family member has their own feelings and roles, and sometimes these can clash. The person's decision to exclude the stepfather might have been based on personal feelings, but it also affected others in the family. It's also important to think about the intention behind the painting. The person wanted to do something nice for their mom, which is commendable. However, the exclusion of the stepfather led to conflict, which might have been avoided with better communication. In terms of right or wrong, it's a bit nuanced. On one hand, the person has the right to express themselves artistically and include whom they feel is appropriate. On the other hand, excluding someone who feels they are part of the family can lead to hurt feelings and conflict. Perhaps a better approach would have been to include the stepfather in the painting or to discuss the composition with the mom beforehand to ensure everyone feels included and valued. In conclusion, while the person's intention was good, the exclusion led to negative consequences. It might have been more considerate to include the stepfather or to communicate their feelings in a constructive way rather than excluding him from the painting.
